info.description: Extract brand identity, company data, screenshots, IAB classifications, and clean page content from any URL.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Your Prefetch API key. Obtain one from the dashboard.

durationMs.description: Time taken to process the request in milliseconds.

CodeColorItem.description: One color scraped from the page's CSS, HTML, or JavaScript.

color.description: The raw value as written on the page.

group.description: Nearest named color, used as the group key.

distance.description: Distance to that named color. 0 is an exact match.

name.description: Tint label within the group, ordered nearest-first.

hex.description: The color as a hex triplet.

source.description: Where the color came from. Present on `screenshot_colors` entries only.

brand_colors.description: The brand palette, built from the logo and brand assets. Always present.

code_colors.description: Colors scraped from the page's code, keyed by nearest named color. Present only when `css=true`, `html=true`, or `javascript=true`. Sources are merged into one map, not split per source.

screenshot_colors.description: Dominant colors sampled from the screenshot. Present only when `screenshotColors=N` is passed.

families.description: Font family names detected on the page.

url.description: Public URL to the logo asset.

width.description: Intrinsic width of the logo in pixels.

height.description: Intrinsic height of the logo in pixels.

primary.description: Best candidate for the primary logo.

secondary.description: Other logo candidates found on the page.

apple_touch_icon.description: URL to the Apple Touch Icon.

BrandAssetItem.description: An image harvested from the site or its social profiles, such as a Twitter banner.

assets.description: Additional brand imagery found on the site and its social profiles.

screenshot_url.description: URL to the page screenshot stored in cloud storage.

SocialLinks.description: Social media profile URLs keyed by platform name.

BrandBlock.description: Brand identity extracted from the page.

domain.description: Normalized domain extracted from the URL.

ClassificationBlock.description: IAB classification of the site. Null in `/enrich` when classification failed.

description.description: Short human-readable description of the website.

long_description.description: Extended multi-sentence description of the website.

stock_tickers.description: Stock ticker symbols associated with the company, if publicly traded.

isins.description: ISIN codes associated with the company's securities.

domain.description: Normalized domain extracted from the URL.

name.description: Legal entity name of the company.

emails.description: Contact email addresses found on the site.

addresses.description: Physical addresses found on the site.
example: 354 Oyster Point Blvd, South San Francisco, CA 94080

screenshot_url.description: Public URL to the screenshot stored in cloud storage.

full_page.description: Whether the full scrollable height was captured.

captured_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the screenshot was taken.

EnrichBrandBlock.description: The same brand block `/brand` returns, without `social_links` — in `/enrich` those live on `company` instead.

EnrichData.description: Combined output from brand, company, and classify extraction. Each block sits under the same key the standalone endpoint uses.

ScrapeMetadata.description: Always present, whatever formats were requested.

robots.description: The page's own robots meta tag.

headings.description: The page's heading outline, up to 100 entries.

content.description: GitHub Flavored Markdown. Links and images are resolved to absolute URLs.

truncated.description: True when the content hit the 1 MB size cap and was cut.

main_content_only.description: True when boilerplate was successfully isolated away. False means the full page body was returned.

text.description: Null when the summary could not be produced; see `warnings`.

internal.description: Links on the same site, subdomains included.

data.description: The extracted object, shaped by your prompt or schema.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems, such as a format that could not be produced.

ScrapePayload.description: The page content fields. Which of them are present depends on the `formats` requested.

domain.description: Bare host, ready for the `url` parameter of every other endpoint.

confidence.description: 0–1. Only `results[0]` can reach 0.8; at or above it, that result is the answer. Below it, a candidate to check.

source.description: `curated`: reviewed brand data. `index`: the name index. `live`: verified against the site during this request.

results.description: Best match first; one entry per domain. Empty when nothing matched.

live_used.description: Whether the live lookup ran — and so whether the request was billed 3 credits.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes, e.g. a live lookup skipped because the service was busy.

lastmod.description: From the sitemap, when the site publishes one.

CrawlScrapeOptions.description: How each crawled page is rendered. The same options `GET /scrape` takes.

max_depth.description: How many links deep to follow from the start URL. Sitemap-seeded pages sit at depth 0, so `max_depth: 0` with `use_sitemap: true` crawls exactly what the sitemap lists and follows nothing.

include_paths.description: Regular expressions matched against a URL's path and query. A URL must match at least one to be crawled.

exclude_paths.description: Regular expressions. A URL matching any of them is skipped. Exclusions win over inclusions.

allow_subdomains.description: Follow links onto subdomains of the start URL.

ignore_query_params.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as one page.

respect_robots_txt.description: Obey the rules in `robots.txt` — Disallow and Crawl-delay. Sitemap discovery happens either way.

use_sitemap.description: Seed the crawl from the site's sitemap as well as from links.

delay_ms.description: Politeness delay between pages. A larger `Crawl-delay` in robots.txt wins.

expires_at.description: After this, the crawl and its pages are no longer readable.

CrawlPage.description: One crawled page. Carries the same fields `GET /scrape` returns, plus the crawl's own bookkeeping.

depth.description: How many links from the start URL. Sitemap-seeded pages are depth 0.

ok.description: False when the page could not be fetched. You are not charged for it.

total.description: Pages the crawl expects to fetch, as currently known. Rises as it discovers more.

next.description: URL for the next page of results, or null when there are no more.

MonitorSchedule.description: Exactly one of `cron` or `text`. A bare string is accepted too, and read as cron when it has five cron fields.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression. Runs must be at least 5 minutes apart.

text.description: A plain-English schedule, converted to cron: "every 30 minutes", "every 15 minutes starting at :07", "hourly", "every 2 hours", "daily", "daily at 9am", "daily at 5:30 PM", "every weekday at 9am", "weekly", "every monday at 8:00", "monthly".

timezone.description: IANA timezone the schedule runs in.

MonitorScrapeOptions.description: How each page is rendered before it is compared — the content-shaping options of `GET /scrape`.

only_main_content.description: Compare the main content only, ignoring navigation, sidebars and footers.

include_links.description: Keep link URLs in the compared markdown.

include_images.description: Keep images in the compared markdown. Off by default: image URLs carry cache-busting hashes that change on every deploy.

include_selectors.description: CSS selectors to compare instead of the detected main content.

exclude_selectors.description: CSS selectors to leave out of the comparison — the way to silence a timestamp or a rotating banner.

modes.description: `markdown` diffs the page text line by line. `json` extracts the fields described by `json_prompt` or `json_schema` on every check and diffs them field by field, so a page is `changed` only when a tracked field changes. Both together report `changed` when either surface changed.

json_prompt.description: For the `json` mode: the fields to track, in plain English.
json_prompt.example: Each plan: name, monthly price, headline features

json_schema.description: For the `json` mode: a JSON Schema for the extraction.

limit.description: Most pages each check crawls. Every page is billed on every check.

max_depth.description: How many links deep to follow from the start URL.

exclude_paths.description: Regular expressions. A matching URL is skipped.

allow_subdomains.description: Follow links onto subdomains of the start URL.

ignore_query_params.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as one page.

use_sitemap.description: Seed each crawl from the site's sitemap as well as from links.

id.description: Stable target id. Generated when omitted; on update, a target watching the same URLs keeps its id — and its snapshots — automatically.

MonitorCrawlTarget.title: Crawl target
MonitorCrawlTarget.description: Re-crawls a site on every check, so pages that appear or disappear are reported as well as pages that change.

id.description: Stable target id. Generated when omitted.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives the events.

headers.description: Extra headers sent with every event, at most 20. `Host`, `Content-Type` and `X-Prefetch-*` are reserved.

metadata.description: Echoed back in every event, up to 4 KB.

secret.description: Signing secret, 16–128 printable characters. Generated when omitted, and kept across updates unless you replace it.

rotate_secret.description: Update only: generate a new signing secret.

goal.description: What you want to be told about, in one plain sentence. With a goal, every changed page is judged against it, and only meaningful changes send a `monitor.page` webhook. 1 credit per page judged.
goal.example: Alert me when a plan price or its included features change

judge_enabled.description: Judge changes against the goal. Default: `true` when a goal is set.

targets.description: What to watch. At most 500 pages per check across all targets.

retention_days.description: How long check history is kept.

MonitorUpdateRequest.description: Any subset of the create fields, plus `status`. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

goal.description: `null` clears the goal and turns judging off.

status.description: Pause or resume. Resuming runs at the next scheduled time; runs missed while paused are not replayed.

secret.description: Verifies the `X-Prefetch-Signature` header on every event.

cron.description: The schedule the monitor runs on — always cron, whatever you submitted.

text.description: The phrase it was created from, if any.

current_check_id.description: The check running right now, if any.

targets.description: Normalised: every target has an id and every option its effective value.

estimated_credits_per_check.description: Upper bound: every page fetched, and judged when a goal is set. A real check costs less — only fetched pages are billed, and only changed ones judged.

estimated_credits_per_month.description: `estimated_credits_per_check` times the runs in an average month.

last_check_summary.description: Counts from the most recent check, or `null` before the first one.

updated_at.description: When the settings last changed. Checks do not touch it.

next.description: URL for the next page of monitors, or null.

status.description: `partial`: some pages errored, or the check stopped early on credits or its time limit — its results are real but incomplete. `skipped_overlap`: the previous check was still running. `skipped_no_credits`: the owning key had no credits or was revoked. Skipped checks are never charged.

estimated_credits.description: Upper bound, computed when the check was queued.

actual_credits.description: What the check was charged: pages fetched at the `/scrape` rate, plus pages judged.

target_results.description: Per target: pages checked, and for crawls whether the crawl ran to completion. Only a complete crawl can report removed pages.

error.description: Why the check is partial, failed or skipped, or what it could not do.

next.description: URL for the next page of checks, or null.

reason.example: The Starter plan's price went from $19 to $24 a month.

text.description: Markdown mode: a unified diff of the page's markdown.

hunks.description: Markdown mode: the same diff as structured hunks.

truncated.description: The diff was larger than the stored cap. The line counts still cover all of it.

too_large.description: The page changed almost entirely, so no line diff was computed.

fields.description: JSON mode: changed fields keyed by JSON path, each `{ previous, current, change }`.

previous_check_id.description: The check the compared snapshot was taken in.

is_meaningful.description: The judge's verdict, or `null` when the page was not judged.

diff.description: For changed pages, and for pages that are new since the first check.

snapshot.description: JSON mode: the full current extraction.

webhook.description: Webhook deliveries for this check, by outcome. `null` when the monitor has no webhook.

Returns progress plus a page of crawled pages, oldest first. Follow `next` until it is null to read every page. Results stay readable for 24 hours after the crawl finishes.

This is also where crawled pages are billed: each call charges for the pages that completed since the previous call, so polling repeatedly never charges twice for the same page.

post.description:
Watches pages on a schedule and tells you what changed. Each check re-fetches every target — a fixed list of URLs (`scrape`) or a whole site (`crawl`) — and compares each page with the previous check: `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed` or `error`, with a diff. Give it a `goal` and every change is judged against it, so only meaningful changes reach your webhook.

The first check records a baseline: every page is `new`, and no `monitor.page` events are sent for it.

**Credit cost: none to create.** Each check bills 1 credit per page it fetches (the `/scrape` rate, 4 on targets tracking `json`), plus 1 per changed page judged against the goal.
